plan.title: bug(hooks,cli): git hooks need npm ci in every linked worktree; old global CLI says 'unknown verb install' for the repair command

narratives.Description: A new linked git worktree has no node_modules, so the git commit hook (the `.githooks/_directive-run.sh` helper) fails on the first commit although the primary checkout already has the pinned runtime, and the Grok and Cursor agent hooks deny every shell call in that state, including the install command their own message names (#6466 is folded in). This story lets the git hook helper run the primary checkout's runtime when the worktree's exact pin equals the version installed there, keeps setup from running for a project the runtime is not installed in, and lets the agent-hook outer admit exactly `npm ci`, `npm install` or `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at the project root when the runtime is missing. It adds no gate, grant, flag or stored state; the missing-runtime exit code on Claude Code and Codex stays separate work.
narratives.Overview:
1. Primary lookup (git hook helper `GITHOOK_HELPER`, deposited as `.githooks/_directive-run.sh`). When `$REPO_ROOT/node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime/dist/bin.js` is missing, the helper runs `git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`. When that command fails (for example on a git without `--path-format`), there is no borrow. Otherwise the helper runs one fixed `node -e` program and passes it two argv values: `$REPO_ROOT` and the printed common directory. No path or file content is put into the program text.
2. The program decides. On Windows it first turns an MSYS path `/<letter>/...` into `<letter>:/...` (the `normalizeHookProjectRoot` rule). It then requires all of these, in order: the common directory is absolute by node's `path.isAbsolute`; its name is `.git`; its parent (the primary checkout) and `$REPO_ROOT` have different real paths; `<primary>/node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime/dist/bin.js` is a file by `statSync`, which follows symlinks, so a pnpm install qualifies; `<primary>/.deft-scratch/materialize-runtime-overlay.json` does not exist; and the worktree pin, read from `$REPO_ROOT/package.json` by the `readRuntimePin` rule (`devDependencies` then `dependencies`, exact semver only, leading `v` removed), equals the `version` in `<primary>/node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime/package.json`. When all hold, it prints the bin path and exits 0. Otherwise it prints one reason line to stderr and exits 1.
3. Borrowed run. The helper prints one stderr line that names the primary checkout and the version, then runs `DIRECTIVE_PROJECT_ROOT="$REPO_ROOT" node "<printed bin.js>" "$@"`. The arguments are unchanged (they already carry `--project-root "$REPO_ROOT"`).
4. No borrow. The helper fails exactly as today (the two stderr lines, exit 1), and also shows the program's reason line: no primary checkout found, no runtime in the primary, overlay marker present, pin not exact, or pin X against installed Y.
5. No setup from a runtime that is not installed in the project. `maybeSelfCompleteSetup` returns without running setup, with a new skip reason `not-installed-here`, only when the checkout that owns the running runtime module (the path rule of `resolveLaunchingCheckoutRootFromPath`) is known, both it and the given project root resolve by `realpathSync`, and the two real paths differ (the same compare as `rootsMatch`). When the owner is unknown (a source run) or either real path cannot be read, behaviour is unchanged. On a borrowed run item 3 sets the project root to the worktree, so the skip fires there, also when the worktree sits inside the primary's tree. Agent hooks are not affected: hook-bin already refuses a different launch root before setup.
6. Agent-hook admit (outer `hostHookOuterSource`). When `hook-bin.js` is missing and the event is `tool.before`, the outer reads the stdin payload. A read failure or a payload that is not a JSON object is denied. The call is allowed only when all of these hold: the tool name, read from the same direct fields as `hookToolName` (`tool_name`, `toolName`, `tool`, `tool.name`, `tool_call.name`, `toolCall.name`), is a shell tool by the `isShellTool` rule; the command, read in the field order of `hookShellCommand`, matches by the `matchPinMismatchRecoveryCommand` rule (simple-command pattern, exact tokens of `PIN_MISMATCH_RECOVERY_COMMANDS`); and every run directory has the same real path as the outer's project root. The run directories are read by the `shellRunDirectories` rule (tool-input `workdir`, `cwd`, `working_directory`, `workingDirectory` first, each present one a non-empty string; otherwise the payload `cwd`). When neither gives a directory, the hook process working directory is the run directory on Grok and Cursor; on Codex there is no run directory and the call is denied. A named directory that is not the project root is denied; there is no fallback from it. The absence of `hook-bin.js` is the precondition; the pin-mismatch-only test is not used. The tool list, command list, field names and pattern are written into the outer source from the core constants when it is generated. The reading functions are a small copy in the outer, and a parity test runs the generated outer and the core functions on the same payload fixtures.
7. Allow output. On Cursor the admitted call prints `{"permission":"allow","code":"shell-op-ready"}` and exits 0. On the other hosts it prints nothing and exits 0. These are the shapes `renderHostDecision` already emits for a plain `tool.before` allow.
8. Deny. Every other call, and every other event, is denied exactly as today (same exit code and output form per host). The reason text on the outer's missing-runtime deny names only the admitted commands, built from the list: "Directive hooks: missing node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime. Run one of `npm ci`, `npm install` or `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` at the project root; other tool calls stay denied until the runtime is installed." The git hook helper and Taskfile messages keep their text.
9. Unchanged: the hook-bin launch-root refusal (AC9.4 / AC9.5), the #6313 admit and its list, and the cheap in-sync check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a linked worktree without `node_modules` whose exact pin equals the version installed in the primary checkout, with no overlay marker, when a commit runs the pre-commit hook, then the hook runs the primary's `bin.js` with `DIRECTIVE_PROJECT_ROOT` and `--project-root` set to the worktree and prints the line that names the primary and the version.
- Given the same worktree with pnpm's symlinked `node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime` in the primary, then the borrow applies.
- Given git prints the common directory as `C:/...` or, on Windows, as `/c/...`, then the program resolves it to the same primary and the borrow applies.
- Given the same worktree and a primary version different from the pin, then the hook exits 1 with today's two lines and a line that names both versions, and does not run the primary's runtime.
- Given a non-exact pin (for example `^0.129.0`), or an overlay marker in the primary, or a primary without the runtime, or a common directory not named `.git`, or a failing `git rev-parse`, then the hook fails as today with the matching reason line.
- Given a `package.json` whose version or path text contains quotes, `$` or backticks, then the program treats them as data and does not run them.
- Given a borrowed run, also with `DIRECTIVE_PROJECT_ROOT` set to the primary in the caller's environment, then `maybeSelfCompleteSetup` returns the skip reason `not-installed-here` and setup writes no file in the worktree or the primary.
- Given a runtime installed in the project on Windows, where the module path rule gives `C:/proj` and the working directory is `C:\proj`, then self-complete behaves as today.
- Given a Grok `run_terminal_command` payload with `tool_input.command` `npm ci` and no directory field, run by a hook whose working directory is the project root while `hook-bin.js` is missing, then the outer exits 0 with empty stdout.
- Given the same on Cursor (a `Shell` payload with the command and no directory field), then the outer prints `{"permission":"allow","code":"shell-op-ready"}` and exits 0.
- Given `npm ci && curl x`, `pnpm install`, `yarn`, `npm ci` with a run directory that is not the project root, a Codex payload without a tool-input directory field, a command found only in a field other than the `hookShellCommand` fields, an MCP or edit tool, or a payload that is not JSON, then the outer denies exactly as today, and the reason names only the three admitted commands.
- A parity test runs the generated outer source and the core functions (`hookToolName` direct fields, `hookShellCommand`, `matchPinMismatchRecoveryCommand`, the `shellRunDirectories` rule) on the same fixtures and gets the same admit result where a payload names a directory.

## In plain English
A new linked worktree (`git worktree add`) has no `node_modules`. Two kinds of hooks then stop the work. The git commit hook looks for the runtime only in the worktree, so the first commit fails, although the primary checkout of the same repository already has the pinned runtime. The Grok and Cursor agent hooks deny every shell call in that state, including the install command that their own message tells the agent to run. The recommended fix has two small parts. The git hook may use the primary checkout's runtime, but only when its version is exactly the worktree's pin. The agent hook lets through only the exact project install commands that the hooks already admit for a pin mismatch (#6313), run at the project root. Everything else still fails closed. The operator folded #6466 into this issue and split the old-CLI wording problem into #6530 (comment 6953560595).

## In plain English

A new linked worktree has no `node_modules`. The git commit hook looks only in that worktree, so the first commit fails even when the main checkout already has the same pinned runtime. In that same state the Grok and Cursor agent hooks refuse every shell call, including the install their own message tells the agent to run.

The recommended shape is right. The git hook may run the main checkout's runtime when the worktree pin equals that installed version and the main checkout has no materialize overlay marker. The agent hook may let through only the three project install commands already admitted for a pin mismatch, and only at the project root. Agent hooks should keep refusing to load the main checkout's hook program. Everything else stays refused.

That shape does not bind as written. One change is required before the git-hook half can bind, and the agent-hook half needs tighter wording so the admit is real on both hosts.

On the version check: the identity the hooks already trust is enough. That is an exact version in the worktree `package.json` against the `version` in the main checkout's installed runtime, with the overlay marker still failing closed. The cheap check does not read the lockfile. A lockfile hash would be a new gate.

On setup repair: it should not run when the runtime is borrowed. An installed tree runs repair once, then the versions match and later commands skip it. A borrowed tree has no installed copy in the worktree, so that skip never arrives. Every commit and every push would run repair again and rewrite project files that are not part of the commit.

On the payload reader: it is the smallest rule that still refuses every other command. The host matcher only knows that the tool is a shell. It cannot see the command text. Letting every shell command through would drop the fail-closed rule. The reader has to use the existing command list and the existing payload fields. Grok and Cursor do not share one allow message. The pin-mismatch function itself will not admit this case, because a missing install leaves the mismatch flags false.

## Findings

### 1. blocks-the-design — A borrowed runtime rewrites the worktree on every hook

Evidence: `packages/runtime/src/bin.ts` lines 16–19, `packages/runtime/src/self-complete.ts` lines 136–168, `packages/core/src/install-health/cheap.ts` lines 59–77, `packages/runtime/src/setup.ts` lines 418–447 and 494–507, read at the dispatch SHA.

G1 runs `node <primary bin.js>` with the hook arguments, as an ordinary command. That entry always calls `maybeSelfCompleteSetup`. The project root for that call is `DIRECTIVE_PROJECT_ROOT` if set, otherwise the process cwd. A git hook's cwd is the linked worktree. A consumer worktree with a pin and committed wiring counts as configured even when `node_modules` is absent (`self-complete.ts` lines 139–144). A missing install is not fail-closed: both versions have to be present before they can mismatch (`cheap.ts` lines 59–68). `cheap.ok` stays false because the installed version is read from the worktree's own `node_modules`. The fast path requires `cheap.ok`, so it never hits. Repair setup runs on every `pre-commit` and every `pre-push`. Repair rewrites wiring (`.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md`, host hooks, the ownership record) and does not stage those writes.

Failure mode: the commit the worktree was opened for also mutates the tree, and the next commit does it again. If `DIRECTIVE_PROJECT_ROOT` points at the main checkout, those writes land there instead. A throw inside setup still fails the commit, so P1 is not reliably relieved either.

Disposition: the borrow can stand. The "run it as a normal command and keep setup parity" limb cannot bind. The borrowed git-hook path has to skip `maybeSelfCompleteSetup`. Teaching the cheap check to pretend the worktree has the package would make later reads treat `node_modules` as present and then fail when they open it. Skipping setup is the smaller rule. Parity would be the right call only if the fast path could succeed with no local install. It cannot.

### 2. sharpens-framing — A missing runtime is outside the pin-mismatch admit

Evidence: `packages/core/src/install-health/cheap.ts` lines 59–68 and 93, `packages/core/src/install-health/recovery-admit.ts` lines 8–14 and 53–73, `packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts` lines 194–211 and 447–456.

`admitPinMismatchRecovery` returns null unless pin ≠ installed is the only fault. With no installed version, both `identityMismatch` and `pinMismatchOnly` are false, and `failClosed` is false unless an overlay marker is present. Calling that function, or reusing "the #6313 rules" including that precondition, denies `npm ci` while `hook-bin.js` is missing. P2 stays.

Disposition: the new precondition is "`hook-bin.js` is absent." The reused pieces are the three token lists, the simple-command pattern, and the run-directory proof. `isPinMismatchOnly` stays on the path that already has a runtime.

### 3. sharpens-framing — The deny text still names commands the list refuses

Evidence: `packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.ts` lines 22–24 and 324–333, `packages/core/src/install-health/recovery-admit.ts` lines 20–24 and 27–31.

The outer's deny reason is the fixed guidance string: run `npm install`, or `pnpm install`, or `yarn`. The admitted list is `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `npm install`, and `npm ci`. A compound command, an extra token, and `yarn` fail the simple-command match. G3 adds a sentence that names the real list and leaves the old sentence in place. An agent that follows `pnpm install` or `yarn` is still denied. That is the bug in #6466 for those two spellings.

Disposition: the recovery clause names only the three admitted commands. `pnpm install` without `--frozen-lockfile`, and `yarn`, are not added to the list.

### 4. sharpens-framing — The payload reader has to use the existing fields

Evidence: `packages/core/src/hooks/classify/paths.ts` lines 176–190, `packages/core/src/hooks/classify/payload.ts` lines 30–42, `packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts` lines 161–186, `packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts` lines 41–49.

Hosts put the command and the working directory in different places. The existing extractor looks at `tool_input.command`, `cmd`, and `shell_command` before the top-level command, and the directory proof uses `workdir`, `cwd`, `working_directory`, and `workingDirectory`, with no Codex fallback. A reader that checks one top-level string misses the Grok install and P2 stays closed. A reader that searches the raw JSON can treat a command sitting in some other field as the command to allow. The outer cannot import the runtime package while that package is missing, so the deposited file has to contain this predicate, generated from the same source as the list.

Disposition: G3's reader is that predicate, including the Codex rule, plus a fixture where `npm ci && …` and a command buried in another field stay denied. A shorter parser does not bind.

### 5. sharpens-framing — Grok and Cursor do not share an allow wire

Evidence: `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` lines 5511–5516 and 5667–5747, `packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.ts` lines 324–333, `packages/core/src/init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts` lines 158–159.

Cursor with `failClosed` treats empty stdout as a hook failure, so a Cursor allow is `{"permission":"allow","code":...}` and exit 0. A Grok tool-before allow with no advisory is exit 0 and empty stdout. Grok's deny is `{"decision":"deny",...}` and exit 0. A Cursor permission object on Grok is not a `decision` of allow or deny. One shared "exit 0" leaves Cursor blocking the install. One shared permission object leaves Grok denying it. Either way one of the two hosts in P2 stays broken.

Disposition: the admitted call uses those two existing wires. No new JSON shape. The admit message is not an advisory (`allowAdvisoryText` only keeps a kill-force reason or a `Warning:`), so Grok's allow stays empty.

### 6. sharpens-framing — The main-checkout lookup can bind the wrong tree, or miss a pnpm install

Evidence: `packages/runtime/src/setup-wiring.ts` lines 1085–1106, `packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.ts` lines 298–305, `packages/core/src/install-health/cheap.ts` lines 25–26 and 50–52, `packages/core/src/install-health/readers.ts` lines 100–131.

Today the helper only resolves the worktree toplevel. G1 then takes the parent of `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`. That flag is not always absolute. A relative print, resolved from the wrong base, either fails closed (P1 stays) or selects some neighboring directory. If that neighbor has a `dist/bin.js` whose package version equals the pin, the hook runs that runtime. The design already requires an absolute path and the name `.git`. It does not say what the helper does with a relative print.

The same limb says the bin is "a regular file." The helper's current test is `[ -f ]`, which follows symlinks. pnpm's `node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime` is usually a symlink into the store. `isRegularFile` in the outer returns false for a symlink. Copying that test onto the git helper means a pnpm main checkout never qualifies, and P1 stays for pnpm.

The version check is a `node -e` program inside the shell helper. A program that pastes the version or the path into the script string turns `package.json` into shell or JS on the commit hook. The pin read has to match `readRuntimePin`: `dependencies` and `devDependencies`, exact semver only, leading `v` stripped. The overlay marker is `.deft-scratch/materialize-runtime-overlay.json` on the main checkout, not a file inside the package.

Disposition: the helper requests an absolute common dir and refuses a relative one. It tests the bin with `[ -f ]`. The version program receives the two `package.json` paths as argv and parses them in node. The overlay check is the main checkout's marker file.

### 7. footnote — Lockfile integrity stays out of this rule

`checkCheapInSync` does not inspect the lockfile (`cheap.ts` lines 50–52). The overlay marker is the existing control for a version string that matches while a tip build is still on disk. Borrowing the main checkout extends that same version trust to other worktrees of the repo. A lockfile hash would be a new gate, which this arc does not add.

- Given the same worktree and a primary version different from the pin, then the hook exits 1 with today's two lines and a line that names both versions, and does not run the primary's runtime.
- Given a non-exact pin (for example `^0.129.0`), or an overlay marker in the primary, or a primary without the runtime, or a common directory not named `.git`, then the hook fails as today with the matching reason line.
- Given a `package.json` whose version or path text contains quotes, `$` or backticks, then the version check treats them as data and does not run them.
- Given a borrowed run, then `maybeSelfCompleteSetup` returns the skip reason `not-installed-here` and no file in the worktree or the primary is written by setup.
- Given a runtime installed in the project (launching checkout equals project root), then self-complete behaves as today.

Node 22.19.0, npm 10.9.3, macOS. Git hooks are from the 0.129.11 template (`.githooks/_directive-run.sh`, `core.hooksPath=.githooks`).

## 1. Git hooks need a full `npm ci` in every linked worktree

`run_directive` looks only at `$REPO_ROOT/node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime/dist/bin.js`, where `REPO_ROOT` is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. A new `git worktree add` has no `node_modules`, so the first commit in it fails:

```
directive hooks: missing <worktree>/node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime/dist/bin.js
Directive hooks: missing node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime. Run npm install or pnpm install (or yarn) in this project.
```

The message is clear. But the fix is a full app install in each worktree. Here that means about 1.5k packages, plus GitHub Packages auth for `@deftai/rivet-os`, only to commit a version bump. We made release and fix worktrees all day, and each one needed `npm ci` before its first commit. The primary checkout's `node_modules` already had the runtime.

Expected: when the worktree has no runtime, the helper falls back to the runtime in the primary checkout (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, then its parent's `node_modules`) if that pin matches `package.json`. If the pin does not match, it fails as it does today.

Related: #6466 (agent hooks, no `node_modules`), #5959 (cwd-relative hook path).

## 2. The old global CLI gives "unknown verb" for the recovery command

AGENTS.md (AC9.7) and the launcher help both give the repair path as `npm i -g @deftai/directive`, then `directive install --repair`. With the old global still installed:

```
$ directive --version
@deftai/directive (engine: @deftai/directive-core@0.126.2; package: @deftai/directive@0.126.2)
$ directive install --repair
directive: unknown verb 'install'
```

A user or agent who skips or loses the first step gets no hint. We ran `npx directive install --repair` and hit this, because `npx directive` resolves to the global CLI (the project has only a `directive-runtime` bin).

Expected: 0.126.x prints that `install` needs the launcher, with `npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest` or `npx @deftai/directive@<pin> install --repair`. If 0.126.x will get no more releases, the AC9.7 text could say to check `directive --version` first.
